text: Every single RLS role starts in the exact same place inside Power BI: Desktop's Manage Roles dialog, sitting right there under the Modeling tab, ready whenever you need it.

Six steps, always followed in this same order. Select New in the Manage roles window. Name the role — no commas allowed anywhere in that name. Pick the specific table you actually want to filter. Write the filter itself, using either the default editor or the DAX editor. And save it. Desktop never lets you assign an actual user to this role from in here — that step only exists over on the service side.

The simplest possible filter you can write is a fixed, static value — something like Region equals West. Only rows where that condition evaluates true stay visible to anyone assigned to this particular role; every other row disappears entirely, not just visually, but from every single visual built on top of this semantic model.

The moment you need something genuinely dynamic instead — filtering based on whoever happens to be signed in at the time — you have to switch over to the DAX editor specifically. Functions like USERNAME, USERPRINCIPALNAME, and CUSTOMDATA are the common patterns people reach for here, and Lesson 82 covers exactly how to use them properly. Static filters are genuinely simple to write, but they need one separate role for every single value — a West role, an East role, a South role, and so on for every region you have. Dynamic filters use just one single role that adapts automatically to whoever's actually signed in.

One role, one filter expression, defined entirely inside Desktop and ready to publish. Lesson 81 covers exactly what happens next, once you've published it — actually assigning real people to that role, over in the service.
